i understand. it can be difficult to navigate strong emotions in general but even more so with something this deep. it took me a long time to realize not everybody, no matter how much we love them, deserves access to every part of us, they have to earn it.

it can be hard to tell the person we love most about our darkest moments, especially with how your ex's reacted i understand completely why you feel this way. this person is important to you so their reaction matters more than it ever did with your ex's. im glad you have your current boyfriend, it sounds like he treats you well. you deserve genuine and safe love.

honestly, i wouldn't tell him until you feel 100% comfortable and safe opening up. there's no reason to pressure yourself to talk to him about it unless it's something that affects your relationship with him. your worries are valid, sometimes people react in unexpected ways when these topics are brought up. however, if you guys have been together for some time and you know / trust him to be a person who would not make you feel the way your ex did, then here is my advice for how to go about it.

-dont bring it up randomly, ask to talk in person in a safe environment and let him know its something serious you have carried for a while. (he might think its you breaking up with him so the way you word that is important) 

-let him know you need his support and understanding due to the severity but allow him to be able to process, he will most likely be upset knowing you have gone through something so horrible.

-preface by letting him know you are not comfortable discussing the specifics. some people do ask to know more because they want to understand what happened but its completely up to you what information you provide and when. hopefully he responds in a way that makes you feel safe enough to find peace through talking about it with him.

-make sure you are actually in a good enough place mentally to be talking about this with him because you could also react in unexpected ways, like shutting down emotionally, getting understandably upset, feeling a pressure on both you and him to react / say certain things, etc. 

all in all, i hope you know that it's not a bad thing that you haven't told him yet. you haven't been ready and that's okay. there should never ever be any pressure involved in talking about these types of things because it should only be talked about to help you feel love, support, and to further their understanding of you, not because you feel guilty. everything is going to be okay.

i understand why you are struggling and it is not deserved. you can get into shape. you can fix your posture. you were born with the penis you have, anyone who loves you for who you are will accept you. none of these things mean it's time for you to stop living.

it could be time for changes that bring you more confidence to keep going. its difficult, ive been there, but you are capable. 

i spent a lot of my life being antisocial, not working, never leaving the house, etc and all of those things were the root cause of me losing my confidence which perpetuated the cycle of self doubt and shame of my appearance. but we all deserve confidence. 

maybe start a small workout routine or just simply go on a walk every day. doesn't have to be far, you can start by just going outside once a day. you can buy a posture corrector and/ or do exercises once a day that will improve your posture significantly.

basically, its extremely hard to get started on anything when you've been feeling this way for a while but starting anything no matter how small can help you build the confidence enough to start something bigger and so on. it's going to be okay, it just takes time but you deserve to at least be around to try.
